title: Wage unrest shuts about 640 factories; two union leaders arrested
excerpt: Garment workers protested for a second day after the wage board meeting was moved to 23 November. Police arrested two federation leaders in Pallabi.

image.alt: An empty courtyard at a garment factory in Tetuljhora, Savar
image.credit: আদিব এহসান / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
About 640 garment factories were disrupted on Tuesday (17 November) as wage protests spread for a second day, The Financial Express reported, citing the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA). Of these, 115 were closed under the "no work, no pay" rule and 525 declared a holiday. Workers took to the streets after the Minimum Wage Board postponed its 16 November meeting to 23 November.

Protests continued on Wednesday. In Ashulia, 132 factories were shut and workers vandalised MK Apparels, The Business Standard reported. Police had arrested Mosammat Sultana Begum, central president of the Green Bangla Garments Workers Federation, and its general secretary Md Ilyas in Pallabi late on Tuesday night, accusing them of threatening owners and stirring up workers.

Police used tear gas and sound grenades on protesters at Jamgora and Narsingpur in Ashulia, and dispersed workers at Hemayetpur in Savar, bdnews24.com's Bangla edition reported. In Kafrul, police and workers clashed after allegations that local BNP leaders had harassed women workers, The Business Standard reported. A 27-year-old worker, Hawa Begum, was hit in the hand by a rubber bullet.

The wage gap

Workers are asking for a minimum wage of Tk 32,000 a month for entry-level workers. The new wage is due to take effect from 1 December, with the first payment in January 2027, according to The Financial Express.

Why it matters

Most garment workers are women, and many live on wages that have trailed prices for years. The arrest of union leaders, factory closures under "no work, no pay" and the use of force at protests raise labour-rights and civic-space concerns for rights groups, legal aid NGOs and organisations working with women workers in Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur.

What to watch

The wage board meeting on 23 November, whether the two federation leaders get bail, and whether more factories close under the "no work, no pay" rule.
